assumptions.summary: Preheated oven and constant oven temperature.
Oven and pan treated as heat reservoirs.
Pan is primary and air secondary heating source.
Flat pans and minimum 36 square inches.
Rack rotation handles oven hot spots.
Brownie mass, density, and volume held constant.
Brownie consistency and no evaporation in the model.
An 8 percent area inflation proxies airflow for square and hexagon packing.

contributions.summary: Defines a two-objective shape-selection route with a worked octagon example.
Compares lattice, tessellation, orientations, and an 8 percent airflow proxy.
Combines diffusion and Newton source terms in a finite-difference simulation.
Uses angle-based corner weights after rejecting two simpler grid allocations.
Uses calorimetry and edge/center temperature series to estimate heat parameters.
Defines magic-number dimensions and the weighted total score.
Reports fixed-grid sensitivity ranges and numerical nonconvergence boundaries.
Returns to conditional, customer-specific selection rather than a universal winner.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Two brownie batches, K-type thermocouple, mass, volume, and timed temperature samples.
Edge and center tables provide calibration series.
104 C plateau points are excluded before fitting.
Density and mass changes are measured but later frozen as constants.
Cupcake literature supplies order-of-magnitude property checks.
K/(c rho), h_pan/(c rho), and h_air/(c rho) become alpha, beta, gamma.

dependency_graph.closure_status: The positive dependency chain is explicit, but appendix code, boundary conditions, surrogate coefficients, and metric equivalence remain unresolved.
edges: experiment -> reduced parameters -> heat field -> heating score
geometry and oven -> packing count -> space score
space score + heating score + p -> weighted total -> recommendation
feedbacks: Sensitivity results return to the calibration and simulation assumptions.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace the 8 percent clearance proxy with measured gap-dependent packing constraints and a reproducible polygon-intersection check.
Re-derive interface signs and impose a stable FTCS or implicit scheme with explicit boundary conditions.
Compute polygon-grid intersection areas directly and validate corner weights against mesh refinement.
Use replicated thermocouple runs, calorimeter heat-loss correction, and uncertainty intervals for c, rho, h_pan, and h_air.
Publish the surrogate equation, fit diagnostics, and a holdout grid before using it for candidate selection.
Use global coupled sensitivity and decision-reversal analysis over alpha, beta, gamma, c-rho, geometry, and time.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A compact tradeoff-to-result abstract may improve retrieval of multiple deliverables; no judge source proves causality.
A stakeholder-facing artifact may make technical outputs actionable; award coexistence is not causal evidence.
Conditional recommendations may be more defensible than a universal winner when the feasible design depends on inputs.

language_observations.summary: Tradeoff, method-provenance, conditional-result, and worked-example routines.

models.summary: MU-A-2013-20559-001: Compute how many equal-area pans fit on one rectangular oven rack and convert the count into a space-utilization score.
MU-A-2013-20559-002: Simulate the brownie temperature field under pan-wall and hot-air heating.

models.section: Determining surface area of each data point
models.summary: MU-A-2013-20559-003: Assign larger pan-contact area to corner grid points while preserving total pan surface area.
MU-A-2013-20559-004: Reduce a simulated temperature history to a zero-to-one even-heating score.
MU-A-2013-20559-005: Estimate specific heat, density, interface coefficients, and reduced thermal parameters for the simulation.
MU-A-2013-20559-006: Approximate heat-simulation efficiency over area and side count for rapid candidate enumeration.

models.section: Final Algorithm for Efficiency and Optimization
models.summary: MU-A-2013-20559-007: Combine space utilization and heating uniformity under a user preference and select the highest-scoring shape.

results_trace.summary: Integer-compatible dimensions create local spacing maxima.
Hit tallies vary with preference and area.
Circle, square, and hexagon dominate different conditions.
No universal shape; rerun for supplied context.

section_map.summary: Four visual paragraphs: tradeoff, two-model route, conditional results, and worked decision example.
Stakeholder brochure translating the technical route into customer inputs and configured pan selection.
One paragraph converts square/circle tradeoff into fixed-area and oven-ratio optimization.
Nine numbered physical and operating assumptions with explicit justifications.
Preference, geometry, thermophysical, interface, and baking parameters.
Packing and heating hypotheses with airflow and candidate-shape conditions.
Lattice, tessellation, orientation, clearance proxy, and space score.
Diffusion, Newton terms, grid approximation, and boundary-volume implementation.
Rejected grid and uniform methods followed by angle-based hybrid weights.
Corner/edge temperature score and zero-to-one interpretation.
Two baking experiments, calorimetry, coefficient fits, and parameter reduction.
Magic numbers, combined objective, hit tallies, and conditional product strategy.
Operating and thermophysical sweeps with numerical convergence boundaries.
Strengths, weaknesses, future improvements, and conclusion.
Four bibliography entries; excluded from positive author-language evidence.

limitations: All 16 physical PDF pages were rendered at 144 DPI and reviewed; no physical page was blank or missing.
Printed technical headers run from Page 1 of 22 through Page 14 of 22; the source refers to appendix code that is absent from the available PDF.
The official 2013 Problem A statement is not present in the corpus; task reconstruction uses the paper's explicit Introduction and Summary restatement.

deliverables: Choose a pan shape with even perimeter heating and high rack-space utilization for fixed area and oven dimensions.
Compute lattice and applicable tessellation counts with airflow clearance.
Simulate heat diffusion and pan/air transfer and compare corner and edge heating.
Calibrate brownie thermophysical parameters from experiments and literature.
Combine space and heating scores under preference p and return a conditional shape recommendation.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: The corpus has no independent official Problem A statement; the paper's task wording and the missing appendix are retained as explicit limits.
task_reconstruction.source: Summary, Introduction to Problem, assumptions, and model sections

verification.summary: Specific heat from a heat-balance relation.
Least-squares fits to filtered edge and center data.
Temperature, height, time, area, and shape sweeps.
Alpha, beta, gamma, and c-rho fixed-grid sweeps.
Plausible output and directional behavior check.

visualization_observations.summary: Stakeholder brochure; useful communication artifact, not quantitative evidence.
Lattice and tessellation diagrams for packing branches.
Regular-polygon geometry interface S, r, R.
Edge and center temperature tables used for coefficient fitting.
Hit tally table by p and candidate shape.

weaknesses.summary: Equation 2 source-term signs conflict with the described heating direction.
Equation 4 equality fails its stated square limit.
Temperature-ratio and E_min/E_max definitions are not reconciled.
A, r, R, k, and K are reused or drift across sections.
The fitted surrogate equation and coefficients are absent.
No replication, uncertainty bands, or interaction analysis.
Appendix code and printed technical pages 15-22 are absent from the source PDF.

writing_logic.summary: Tradeoff -> two models -> experimental provenance -> conditional result -> worked decision.
Customer pains -> technical benefit -> inputs -> configured recommendation.
Square/circle contrast -> fixed area and oven ratio -> optimization.
Symbol groups -> candidate intuition -> model decomposition.
Geometry cases -> clearance proxy -> count -> space score.
Governing laws -> numerical barrier -> grid -> surface correction -> score.
Parameter need -> experiments -> failure/exclusion -> fit -> literature -> reduction.
No universal winner -> magic boundary -> weighted objective -> tally -> strategy.
Validity question -> baseline -> ranges -> direction -> convergence/practical caveat.
Method or physics omission -> impact -> remedy.
Metric and measurement needs -> physical interfaces.
Model recap -> evidence recap -> conditional recommendation.
